app.name: OUTPOST
app.tagline: You run a Moon or Mars base. You don't have enough power for everything — so every choice costs something.
app.disclaimer: A learning game that uses real NASA data. Numbers marked “game model” are simplified for play.
app.footer: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

site.moonDesc: 10 sols near the lunar south pole. The long night cuts your solar power. Good for a first mission.
site.marsDesc: 12 sols on Mars. A dust storm can dim the Sun for days, and help from Earth is minutes away.

term.solDef: A “sol” is one day on your base. A day on Mars is 24 hours 39 minutes long.
term.doseDef: Radiation is invisible energy from the Sun and space that can harm the body. “Dose” is how much the crew soaked up, measured in mSv.
term.shieldDef: Shielding is material (like piled-up soil) that blocks space radiation and protects the crew.
term.microDef: In space things float because gravity is very weak. This is called microgravity.

home.step1: Each sol, split your power between the crew's needs.
home.step2: Press “Next sol” to see what happens.
home.step3: Keep the crew alive and finish the science.
home.demoHint: The game plays a short Moon mission by itself.
home.ideaBody: Power is tight. Spend it on air and food, or on shielding before a solar storm, or on science to finish the mission. You can’t do it all — and that’s the real job of a mission planner.
home.dataBody: Your solar storms come live from NASA’s space-weather service. The radiation, the Martian day, the Earth–Mars radio delay — all real numbers, all sourced in the game.
home.readyBody: Pick a base and run your first mission.

game.nominal: All quiet. A good sol to do science.
game.splitHint: Give power to what the crew needs most. You can't fund everything — that's the hard part.
game.commsMoon: Earth is about 1.3 seconds away — help comes fast.
game.commsMars: Earth is {min} minutes away by radio. You must decide on your own.
game.hintMars: Message sent to Earth. The reply takes {min} minutes — on Mars you can't wait, decide now.
game.hintLost: Signal lost in the storm — no help from Earth this sol.
game.tipShield: a solar storm is coming — raise your shielding.
game.tipLife: life support or food is low — top it up before it runs out.
game.tipScience: all is calm — a great sol to run science.

need.lifeTip: Makes the air to breathe and cleans the water.
need.shieldTip: Blocks space radiation. Raise it before a solar storm.
need.scienceTip: Does experiments. This is your mission goal.
need.crewTip: Rest and exercise so the crew stays healthy.

meter.lifeHint: Air and water. If it hits zero the crew can't breathe.
meter.foodHint: If it hits zero the crew goes hungry.
meter.healthHint: Falls when a solar storm gets through a weak shield.

preset.survivalTip: Life support, food and shielding first.
preset.shieldTip: Raise the shield fast before a storm.

hazard.flareTip: A real solar flare ({cls}) is hitting. If your shield is low, the crew gets a radiation dose.
hazard.flareComing: A solar storm is coming in {in} sol(s) — flare class {cls}. Raise your shielding!
hazard.dustTip: Dust blocks the Sun, so you get less power this sol.
hazard.nightTip: The long lunar night means little solar power this sol.

report.title: Mission report
report.noKey: A smooth mission — no single moment stands out.

data.title: Real NASA data
data.lead: This game uses real NASA numbers, not made-up ones. Solar storms come live from NASA's space-weather service when you're online. Here is every real fact and where it comes from.
data.liveNote: When you start a mission and you're online, the game asks NASA's DONKI service for real recent solar flares and uses them as your storms. Offline, it uses real flares from NASA's archive instead — never fake ones.
data.model1: How fast each resource rises or falls per unit of power is a game model, tuned so choices feel fair.
data.model2: The mission is a few sols long so you can finish in minutes; a real mission lasts months or years.
data.model3: Radiation doses are based on real daily rates but rounded for a simple meter.

fact.cruiseDose: Radiation on the trip to Mars

fact.dust: What a Mars dust storm does to solar power
fact.flareClass: Solar flare classes, weakest to strongest

demo.label: Demo
demo.s1: A Moon mission. We spread power across life support, food and shielding — and save some for science.
demo.s2: A real solar storm is coming. We pour power into shielding so the crew stays safe.
demo.s3: The storm hits — but the shield holds. Now back to science.
demo.s4: The long lunar night cuts our power, so we protect life support first.
demo.s5: Mission report: the crew came home safe and the science got done.

tutorial.title: How to play
tutorial.lead: A quick guide — about one minute.
tutorial.s1b: You run a base on the Moon or Mars for a few sols — space days. Your job: keep the crew alive and finish the science.
tutorial.s2b: Life support, shielding, food and crew health must stay out of the red. If one hits zero, the mission is over.
tutorial.s3b: Every sol you get a little power. Tap the + and − buttons to give it to what the crew needs most.
tutorial.s4b: Power you spend on shielding is power you did not spend on science. Every choice costs something — that is the hard part, and the fun part.
tutorial.s5b: Real solar storms from NASA hit on some sols. Raise your shield BEFORE one arrives, or the crew gets a dose of radiation.
tutorial.s6b: When your plan is ready, press “Next sol” to see what happens. At the end you get a mission report. Ready, astronaut?
